increment_paragraph: **CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE** (census only; rule 38, contract specification C04.6.2 and C06.5, grammar G05d/G05e; USER DIRECTIONS 2026-11-03, verbatim: "We have to clarify why the difference is caused on our contracts." and "The Fluent Bit's caller tests sometimes check the incorrect assertions so we need to pay attention for the assertions and actual returning values of Fluent Bit functions."; USER DECISION 2026-11-03 (verbatim): "Yes, as recommended"): a reproducible census (`census/census.py --check`, bound to each tree's SHA-256 digest at 66910c10, 046accf6, 34155955 and the corpus's Monkey source) reads every backend body of `mk_event_channel_create` and `mk_event_timeout_create` through their helpers and classifies every caller test from the body-derived result set. Fluent Bit builds the epoll backend, the corpus analyses Monkey's libevent build. In every backend the bodies alone make 0 exactly the channel's success, so the contract's `#result == 0` / `!= 0` (D3) is exact; the result set is {-1, 0} only with the C library's result sets for epoll (`pipe`, `epoll_ctl`; the body alone allows every int), so Fluent Bit's nine `ret == -1` tests are correct but redundant and rule 38 cannot decide them from Monkey's body. Immediate-result tests per Fluent Bit tree (046accf6): 23 exact, 13 redundant, 1 wrong (Monkey mk_server.c:585 `timeout_fd > 0`), 1 untested (Monkey test lib_server.c); no `src/` test of an immediate result is wrong (26: 17 exact, 9 redundant). Stored-result tests: 20 wrong per tree, each reading descriptor 0 as absent (strongest: flb_input_collector_destroy's `coll->fd_timer > 0` against its own -1 sentinel), source readings only. No row can move today: every named creation is refused at the access gate first. By the user's decision the implementation (libc result sets as flexible libc contracts under `libc-c-standard-abi`; a range derived at `pin --bounds` from the configured backend's body chain with the helper sites in the lock) moves to CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE-CHECKED. No contract, gateway, Lean or test change; no prediction or measurement (nothing analysed changes). Report: [docs/reports/cell-guard-result-range/README.md](../../reports/cell-guard-result-range/README.md).

ledger.why: DISCHARGED as a census by CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE (docs/reports/cell-guard-result-range/README.md): the census derives every backend body's result set of mk_event_channel_create and mk_event_timeout_create through their helpers at 66910c10, 046accf6, 34155955 and the corpus's Monkey source, classifies every caller test of the immediate and stored result (exact / redundant / wrong / untested) from those bodies only, bound to source digests, and answers why the contract and the callers differ (the contract's `== 0` split is exact from the bodies alone; `== -1` equals it only under the C library's result sets in the epoll build Fluent Bit uses). The implementation (declared range, rule 38's reading, Lean, fixtures, measurement) moved to CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE-CHECKED by USER DECISION 2026-11-03 (verbatim): "Yes, as recommended".

ledger.title: A pin-derived, libc-grounded result range lets rule 38 decide `ret == -1` callers of Monkey's channel creator
ledger.text: Registered by CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE on USER DECISION 2026-11-03 (verbatim): "Yes, as recommended" (accepting the report's section 4: Q1 (a), Q2 (ii), Q3). The census (docs/reports/cell-guard-result-range/census/) shows that Monkey's `_mk_event_channel_create` returns {-1, 0} in the epoll configuration Fluent Bit builds only with POSIX `pipe` and Linux `epoll_ctl` returning 0 or -1 (the body alone allows every int; kqueue, select and poll [MIN, 0]; libevent, the corpus's analysed build, {-1, 0} from the body alone), that no system or slice run analyses a Monkey unit, and that the corpus checks only libevent. Fluent Bit's `ret == -1` channel tests (flb_engine.c:1168/:1246, flb_input_thread.c:262/:275/:287, flb_output_thread.c:238/:537/:553, flb_scheduler.c:794 at 046accf6) are therefore redundant only under the C library's result sets and stay undecided. DISCHARGE: (a) the C library's documented result sets the derivation reads (`pipe`, `epoll_ctl`; `kevent`, `open`, `timerfd_create`, `evutil_socketpair` where a backend reads them) declared in quirin-provider-libc as flexible result ranges under the standing assumption `libc-c-standard-abi` (a flexible mode for libc result ranges, today absent from bounds contract v1), and the range check reading a call result through a declared range in force and through an in-unit helper's summary (a local assigned only such values included); (ii) `nonnull_result_range(-1, 0)` declared on `mk_event_channel_create` (and on any other cell-bearing Monkey declaration whose split constant differs from its callers' tests; `mk_event_timeout_create`'s callers all test `== -1`, which is exact) and derived at `quirin-audit pin --bounds` time from the configured backend's body chain at each reviewed revision, the lock recording the sites of every helper the derivation read (`_mk_event_channel_create`, `_mk_event_add` in mk_event_epoll.c), so that the range is in force exactly where the audited source matches, known before any unit is analysed; `providers/contracts.py sync` and the reviewed lock diffs in the same commit; rule 38's result-guard reading (legacy_descriptor_cells.rs and the rule-38 package) using a range only while in force (a caller's test decides a contract class exactly when, within the range, the test's class equals the contract's; a withdrawn, unchecked, refuted or held range changes nothing, never Safe on an assumed range); a test the census classes wrong (a value of the result set misclassified, or a constant the body never returns) stays undecided or refuses, never smoothed over; Lean parity (a module proving the class equivalence under a range and that an out-of-force range never decides; no placeholders, no project axioms) with vectors shared with Rust; fixtures asserting the full diagnostic vector for both caller spellings at a channel creator, a refuted range, a range out of force and an out-of-range test constant; the census rerun (`--check`) at the pinned trees; PREDICTION.md before implementation and a declared measurement. No row is expected to move until the access gate admits the creations: every named creation (flb_engine_start :1168/:1237/:1246, input_thread_instance_create :262/:275/:287, flb_sched_create :794, Monkey mk_sched_launch_worker_loop :365 and mk_server_create :115/:136) keeps `indirect memory access is outside the resource projection` before rule 38 reads its result.

ledger.title: Candidate defects: guards that read a Monkey creator's descriptor 0 as absent, and timer arms that ignore a failed registration
ledger.text: Registered by CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE (census part 4, docs/reports/cell-guard-result-range/census/census.json). Source readings only; nothing is filed upstream. A creator's descriptor result is >= 0 on success under the C library's result sets, so a later guard that reads descriptor 0 as absent misreads a success value; each is reachable only when descriptor 0 is free in the process (stdin closed at start; flb_utils_set_daemon closes only stdout and stderr). Not tracked elsewhere (046accf6 lines): flb_input_collector_destroy (flb_input.c:3145) `coll->fd_timer > 0`, the strongest, since the holder's own absent value is -1 (:2242, :3181): a COLLECT_TIME timer on descriptor 0 is never destroyed and the collector holding its registered event is freed while the loop still holds it; flb_engine_started and flb_engine_failed (flb_engine.c:1034, :1048) `config->ch_notif[1] <= 0` report a write end on 0 as no channel; flb_engine_start's shutdown timer (flb_engine.c:1497 `<= 0` creates it again, :1563 `> 0` never destroys it); flb_sp_window_destroy (flb_sp.c:670) `task->window.fd > 0`; Monkey (Fluent Bit's lib/monkey and the corpus's Monkey): mk_server_worker_loop never tests its timer at mk_server.c:502 and destroys it only under `timeout_fd > 0` (:585), mk_server_lib_notify_event_loop_break (:630) and mk_server_lib_notify_started (:648) read a write end on 0 as no channel, and the test program test/lib_server.c:160 overwrites `ret` (:167) before testing it. Also Monkey's timer arms that return a descriptor whose registration failed: epoll without timerfd (:319), select (:253), poll at 66910c10 (:252, fixed at 046accf6) and libevent (:369, :375, the corpus's analysed configuration). The channel destroyers' `> 0` ends are appended to CELL-PROTOCOL-PER-END-GUARDS. DISCHARGE: per site, an upstream change with a pinned rerun of the census showing the guard reads the holder's own sentinel, or a recorded decision to leave it unreported; a native scenario (descriptor 0 closed at spawn, as W43-DESC-FLB-CONFIG-DATA-PIPE-ZERO-GUARD did) before any is presented as observed.

ledger.title: event_loop.qv names epoll as the analysed configuration; the corpus analyses Monkey's libevent build
ledger.text: Registered by CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE. providers/qcore-provider-libevent/contracts/monkey/event_loop.qv's header calls the epoll backend (mk_event_epoll.c) "the analysed configuration". The corpus analyses Monkey's own build, which defines MK_EVENT_LOOP_LIBEVENT (monkey-build/include/monkey/mk_core/mk_core_info.h), so the analysed body is the libevent backend; epoll is Fluent Bit's production configuration (no MK_EVENT_LOOP_* define, a Linux build), which no route analyses. The declarations' states hold for all five backends (the census's part 1). DISCHARGE: the comment corrected with `providers/contracts.py sync` (a comment-only change leaves the normalised text and the pins unchanged; confirm with `pin --check`).

ledger.title: Rule 38's W43 validity reading assumes a timer result of -1 or >= 0, which only the C library's result sets give
ledger.text: Registered by CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE. Rule 38 reads a descriptor witness (`!= -1` / `== -1` guard) through W43's validity `facts` table (legacy_descriptor_custody.rs), which reads `fd < 0` as `fd == -1` and `fd >= 0` as `fd != -1` "for a descriptor whose values are -1 or >= 0". The census finds `mk_event_timeout_create`'s result set {-1} u [0, MAX] only with the C library's result sets (`timerfd_create`, `open`, `pipe`, `evutil_socketpair`, `epoll_ctl`); from the bodies alone it is every int in every backend (`return timer_fd` / `fd` / `fd[0]` after a test of -1 only). No Fluent Bit `src/` site tests the timer that way today (every test is `== -1`, exact); only Monkey's test programs (`fd >= 0`) do. DISCHARGE: the validity reading at a cell witness taken only from a result set in force under CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE-CHECKED's (a) and (ii) (a declared, pin-derived range), or a recorded decision that the descriptor value set is part of the standing libc assumption, with Lean parity and fixtures.

APPENDED (CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE, 2026-11-03, census part 4): read against the creator's body-derived result set, every `> 0` end test here (flb_input.c:1311/:1315, flb_output.c:615/:619, flb_input_thread.c:210/:213/:218/:221, flb_config.c:617/:625/:627 at 046accf6) is a WRONG test of a stored result: the absent value is calloc's 0 and descriptor 0 is a success value, so an end on descriptor 0 is never closed (a candidate defect, source reading only; reachable when descriptor 0 is free at creation). The other candidates of the same class are CELL-GUARD-DESCRIPTOR-ZERO-READ-AS-ABSENT.

APPENDED (CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE, 2026-11-03): the census finds the same guard class over Monkey creators' results in flb_config_exit itself (`config->ch_manager[0] > 0`, `config->ch_notif[0] > 0`, `config->ch_notif[1] > 0`, flb_config.c:617/:625/:627 at 046accf6), in flb_engine_started/flb_engine_failed (`ch_notif[1] <= 0`), flb_input_collector_destroy (`coll->fd_timer > 0` against a -1 sentinel) and elsewhere; source readings, listed in CELL-GUARD-DESCRIPTOR-ZERO-READ-AS-ABSENT and CELL-PROTOCOL-PER-END-GUARDS.

AMENDED (CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE, 2026-11-03, census only): the creators' `ret == -1` mismatch registered as CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE is explained by the bodies: the contract's `#result == 0` split is exact from every backend's body alone, and `== -1` equals it only under the C library's result sets in the epoll build Fluent Bit uses (no route analyses that body; the corpus analyses Monkey's libevent build). By USER DECISION 2026-11-03 (verbatim): "Yes, as recommended" the decision moves to CELL-GUARD-RESULT-RANGE-CHECKED (libc result sets under libc-c-standard-abi, a range derived at pin --bounds time). No Fluent Bit `src/` test of a creator's immediate result is wrong (26: 17 exact, 9 redundant).
